Graph of the velocity v(t), in meters per second, for t from 0 to 7 seconds: a segment from (0, -2) up to (2, 4), a horizontal segment to (5, 4), and a segment down to (7, -2)

items.q: A particle moves along the $x$-axis with position $x(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t$ meters at time $t$ seconds, as graphed. Find its velocity at $t = 2$, with units.

mistakes.why: That is $x(2)$, the position. Velocity is the derivative of position.
The sign matters for velocity: $v(2) = -3$ means the particle moves left. 3 is the speed.

items.q: Find the acceleration of the particle at $t = 3$, with units.

mistakes.why: That is $v(3)$. The acceleration is the derivative of velocity, $a(t) = 6t - 12$.

why.correct: $a(t) = v'(t) = 6t - 12$, so $a(3) = 6$ meters per second per second.

items.q: At $t = 2.5$ seconds, is the particle speeding up or slowing down?
options: Slowing down, because $v(2.5) < 0$ and $a(2.5) > 0$
Speeding up, because $a(2.5) > 0$
Speeding up, because $v(2.5)$ and $a(2.5)$ are both negative
Slowing down, because $v(2.5) < 0$

why.correct: $v(2.5) = 3(2.5)^2 - 12(2.5) + 9 = -2.25$ and $a(2.5) = 3$. They have opposite signs, so the speed is decreasing: slowing down.
options: $v(2.5) = -2.25$ and $a(2.5) = 3$: opposite signs.
A positive acceleration speeds the particle up only if it is moving in the positive direction.
The sign of $v$ alone gives the direction of motion, not whether speed grows.

items.q: On which interval is the particle moving to the left?

why.correct: Moving left means $v(t) < 0$. Since $v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$, that is $1 < t < 3$, where the graph of $x$ falls.
options: $v$ is positive for $t > 3$; the acceleration is positive on $2 < t < 4$.
$v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3) < 0$ there, and the graph of $x$ falls.
The particle moves right until $t = 1$.
$v > 0$ there: the position increases.

items.q: At which times does the particle change direction, and why?
options: $t = 2$, because $a(2) = 0$
$t = 0$ and $t = 3$, because $x = 0$ there
$t = 1$ and $t = 3$, because $v$ changes sign there
$t = 1$ and $t = 3$, because $x(t) = 4$ or $x(t) = 0$ there

why.correct: The direction changes where $v$ changes sign. $v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$ changes sign at $t = 1$ (positive to negative) and $t = 3$ (negative to positive).
options: A zero of $a$ is where the velocity stops falling; the particle still moves left.
Being at the origin says nothing about the direction of motion.
$v$ goes from positive to negative at 1 and from negative to positive at 3.
The right times, but the reason must be about $v$: it changes sign.

items.q: The graph shows the velocity $v(t)$ of a particle moving along a line, in meters per second. Find the acceleration at $t = 1$, with units.

mistakes.why: That is $v(1)$, the height of the graph. Acceleration is its slope.

why.correct: $a(1) = v'(1)$, the slope of the first segment: $\frac{4 - (-2)}{2 - 0} = 3$ meters per second per second.

items.q: Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at $t = 6.5$?
options: Slowing down, because the acceleration is negative
Slowing down, because the velocity is negative
Neither, because the velocity is close to 0
Speeding up, because $v(6.5)$ and $a(6.5)$ are both negative

why.correct: $v(6.5) = 19 - 19.5 = -0.5$ and $a(6.5) = -3$. Same signs mean the speed $|v|$ is increasing: speeding up.
options: Negative acceleration slows the particle only while it moves in the positive direction.
The sign of $v$ alone gives the direction, not the change in speed.
A small speed can still be growing; compare the signs of $v$ and $a$.
$v(6.5) = -0.5$ and $a(6.5) = -3$: the same sign.

items.q: At which times does the particle change direction?
options: Just $t = \frac{19}{3}$, where $v$ turns negative

why.correct: Solve $v = 0$: $3t - 2 = 0$ gives $t = \frac{2}{3}$, and $19 - 3t = 0$ gives $t = \frac{19}{3}$. $v$ changes sign at both.
options: $v$ crosses the axis there, changing sign each time.
There the acceleration changes, but $v = 4 > 0$: the particle keeps moving right.
Those are the ends of the interval, not sign changes of $v$.
$v$ also changes sign at $t = \frac{2}{3}$, from negative to positive.

items.q: Which describes the motion of the particle on $2 < t < 5$?
options: At rest, because the acceleration is 0
Moving right at a constant speed of 4 meters per second
Speeding up, because the velocity is at its largest
Moving left, because the graph of $v$ is flat

why.correct: On $2 < t < 5$, $v(t) = 4 > 0$ and $a(t) = 0$: the particle moves right at a steady 4 meters per second.
options: Zero acceleration means constant velocity, here 4 m/s, not zero velocity.
$v = 4$ throughout, and $a = 0$.
The velocity is constant there, so the speed does not change.
A flat graph of $v$ above the axis means steady motion to the right.

items.q: What is the speed of the particle at $t = 7$, in meters per second?

mistakes.why: That is the velocity. Speed is its absolute value, never negative.

why.correct: $v(7) = -2$, so the speed is $|v(7)| = 2$ meters per second (moving left).

items.q: A particle has position $x(t) = te^{-t}$. Find its velocity $v(t)$.

mistakes.why: That multiplies the two derivatives. Use the product rule on $t \cdot e^{-t}$.
The derivative of $e^{-t}$ is $-e^{-t}$ by the chain rule.

items.q: For the position $x(t) = te^{-t}$, find the acceleration $a(t)$.

mistakes.why: That is $v(t)$. Differentiate once more to get $a(t)$.

items.q: A particle has velocity $v(4) = -5$ meters per second. Which is true at $t = 4$?
options: It is moving right at a speed of 5 meters per second
It is moving left at a speed of $-5$ meters per second
It is moving left at a speed of 5 meters per second
It is slowing down, because the velocity is negative

why.correct: The sign of the velocity gives the direction (left), and its absolute value gives the speed (5 m/s).
options: A negative velocity means motion in the negative direction.
Speed is never negative; the sign belongs to the velocity.
Negative velocity means leftward; speed is $|-5| = 5$.
Slowing down depends on the signs of both $v$ and $a$.

items.q: At $t = 3$, a particle has $v(3) = -4$ and $a(3) = -2$. The particle is
options: slowing down, because $a(3)$ is negative
slowing down, because $v(3)$ is negative
at rest, because $v(3)$ and $a(3)$ are both negative
speeding up: $v(3)$ and $a(3)$ share a sign

why.correct: Speeding up when $v$ and $a$ share a sign; slowing down when they differ. Here both are negative: speeding up while moving left.
options: A negative acceleration speeds up a particle moving in the negative direction.
The sign of $v$ alone gives direction only.
At rest means $v = 0$; here the particle moves left.
Both negative: the acceleration points the way the particle moves.

items.q: A particle moves with position $x(t) = 2\cos(\pi t)$. Find $v\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$.

mistakes.why: The chain rule factor $\pi$ from the inside $\pi t$ is missing.

why.correct: $v(t) = -2\pi\sin(\pi t)$ by the chain rule, so $v\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -2\pi\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = -2\pi$.

items.q: A particle's velocity satisfies $v(4) = 0$, and $v$ changes from positive to negative at $t = 4$. Which must be true? Select all that apply.
options: The particle is at rest at $t = 4$
The particle changes direction at $t = 4$
The particle is at the origin at $t = 4$

why.correct: $v(4) = 0$ means at rest; the sign change means a change of direction. Neither fixes $a(4)$ or $x(4)$.
options: $v(4) = 0$ means the particle is momentarily at rest.
$v$ changes sign there: from moving right to moving left.
Nothing forces $a(4) = 0$: as $v$ falls through 0, $a(4)$ is usually negative.
$v = 0$ says nothing about the position $x(4)$.
